A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and retained equations, results, and relocated figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy-model training experiments, numerical calculations, and evaluations of Pythia checkpoints on FineWeb.

after.justification: v2 retains those results and adds structured-data experiments, MNIST training results, OLMo evaluations, and a comparative fitting analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed teacher–student softmax model, KL/cross-entropy objective, aligned-student framework, and existing residual-layer extension remain unchanged. The added networks and data serve as validation experiments rather than revisions of the proposed mechanism.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST digit classification and synthetic teachers with power-law logit-covariance spectra (Sections D.6 and D.8), substantially extending the represented tasks and data conditions. OLMo is evaluated on the retained FineWeb dataset, so its addition alone does not expand dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Section D.9 introduces an independently fitted training-step scaling law as a comparator to dynamic-time fitting. In v1, the step-based comparison reused the offset fitted using dynamic time; v2 fits a separate offset and exponent for the step-based alternative (Figure 29).

E3.justification: New protocols include full-batch MNIST training with a width-10 MLP and Adam, covariance-exponent sweeps from 0 to 2, and OLMo-2 1B/7B/13B checkpoint evaluation. The new fitting comparison uses identical Pythia points, independently fitted offsets, and R-squared to quantify collapse quality.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct robustness test of whether power-law data structure changes the scaling exponent (Figure 23). It also addresses possible bias in the original time-variable comparison through independent refitting (Figure 29). Existing optimizer, initialization, weight-decay, and residual-model analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report fitted-exponent uncertainties, including those in Figure 3 and the Pythia plots; the OLMo results follow the same practice. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure is documented. The added R-squared values assess fit quality.

E6.justification: New results include approximately one-third scaling across structured-data conditions, a MNIST training-loss exponent of 0.35, and OLMo exponents of 0.35 ± 0.01, 0.30 ± 0.01, and 0.36 ± 0.02 for 1B, 7B, and 13B. Figure 29 reports R-squared values of 0.98 for dynamic time and 0.93 for steps. Retained Pythia exponents are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 replaces an asserted analytic expansion with an energy-gap derivation, explicit continuity and positive-density assumptions, and discussion of degeneracy and alternative universality classes. Gradient outer-product expressions are corrected. However, new Equation 80 contains an indexing error: its i-indexed sum uses eta_t rather than eta_i.

C1.justification: The central mechanism and one-third prediction remain, but universality is qualified as generic rather than inevitable throughout the intermediate regime. Appendix A.3 gives this qualification substantive meaning by allowing different exponents when the leading coefficient vanishes.

C2.justification: v2 identifies positive energy-gap density near tied leading outputs as an applicability condition and acknowledges that it is difficult to verify in LLMs. It distinguishes continuity from analyticity, discusses other universality classes, and recognizes the potential unfairness of v1's collapse comparison. These materially refine the mechanism's interpretation and boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 documents the structured-teacher construction, MNIST architecture and optimizer settings, OLMo model/script identifiers, and the Pythia learning-rate schedule. It removes v1's paragraph specifying FP16 loading, automatic device placement, and caching. The existing code-access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MNIST, OLMo, and Liu et al.'s residual-model work, plus a paragraph interpreting earlier reported scaling exponents. The established positioning against data-structure explanations remains intact; the publication update to an existing reference is bibliographic.

P1.justification: The overall section structure and most existing prose are retained. Changes include targeted wording revisions, a reorganized transition from toy models to LLMs, new appendix subsections and explanatory notes, expanded acknowledgements, and an impact statement.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is rebuilt as a four-panel display incorporating v1's appendix Figure 26, with changed vertical scaling in the logit panel. New Figures 23, 26, 29, and 30 display structured-data, MNIST, fitting-comparison, and OLMo results. Most other figures are retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central justification: Appendix A.3 derives previously asserted low-temperature behavior under explicit assumptions, while Figure 29 addresses the potentially unfair comparison by independently fitting both time parameterizations. Structured-data, MNIST, and OLMo results broaden validation. These gains outweigh local notation and documentation regressions, although the LLM gap-density condition and rotation explanation remain unverified.
